sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **8 of the official questions in Circles are this one** — 0 Easy, 7 Medium, 1 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question gives an angle in radians and asks for degrees, or the other way round.
- Harder versions hide the angle inside a difference or an expression.

sections.heading: The method
body: - Degrees to radians: multiply by π/180.
- If the angle is a difference or an expression, convert the whole thing at once.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type the radian value times 180/π, or the degree value times π/180, and Desmos gives the decimal.
To match a choice written in terms of π, divide your result by π to see the coefficient.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You multiply by the wrong factor (π/180 when you need 180/π).
Or you leave π in a degree answer.
Or you think of π as 3.14 degrees instead of 180°.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You multiply by the wrong factor (π/180 when you need 180/π).
Or you leave π in a degree answer.
